16:35 Local Time, 10:35 GMT, 16:05 IST: Another absorbing day of Test cricket. Jangoo and Greaves were accumulating runs happily early this morning but the second new ball was the turning phase. Hasan Mahmud struck twice in two balls to get rid of Jangoo, the centurion, and Chase. He almost got a hat-trick but an inside edge saved Bishop (reviewed successfully for lbw). The Windies tail did wag though and they added some handy runs to take their total over 350. In response, Bangladesh were in some early trouble. Nayeem opened the batting instead of Shadman (who twisted his ankle earlier in the day and was taken for a MRI scan) but he was nipped out early by Seales. Tanzid played a loose shot and was caught brilliantly by Wickham at covers.

The visitors continued to bowl in tight channels and the runs were hard to come by. Shamar knocked Shanto over early in the final session courtesy a jaffa. Hridoy looked tentative early on but looked much more assured as his innings progressed while Mushfiqur dug in too. Both ensured that they didn't allow West Indies to dent them further. The hosts are in a tricky position and are in need of a substantial partnership. There's been early moisture on the surface in the morning and the Windies seamers will be eyeing to exploit it. Join us tomorrow for Day 3. Goodbye for now.

09:00 Local Time, 03:00 GMT, 08:30 IST: Hello and welcome to our coverage of Day 3 of this second Test between Bangladesh and West Indies. So far in this match, a bunch of wickets have fallen in the morning session - 3 on the first day, and 4 on the second. An important factor in that was the presence of a new ball on both those days. Combined with the early morning moisture, the new ball nipped around and made life difficult for batters. However, the ball West Indies currently have is already 40 overs old. And this pitch hasn't responded much to the older ball. Let's see if they can extract some help this morning.
Hasan Mahmud: Five-for is always special. When it happens at home, it's different.

Justin Greaves: Really love Test cricket so doing whatever I can for the team. Don't think it's a pitch where you can blast people out. It's about being patient. Always good batting with Amir. Very very good friend of mine. He made it very easy for me as well. He's been batting really well.

Pitch and conditions | Ian Bishop: First thing about the overhead conditions is this is the hottest morning of the Test so far. Barely negligible (footmarks). That means the batters still have a fair level of comfort against spinners. Cracks are visible but still haven't opened up in any significant way.
It's a bright and sunny morning in Sylhet as the players make their way out.
